For background, in ASVS v4.0.3 we had requirement that combined 3.7.2 and 3.7.4:
> v4.0.3-5.1.5 Verify that URL redirects and forwards only allow destinations which appear on an allow list, or show a warning when redirecting to potentially untrusted content.	

Via #1603 it was split, also note, that the level for them is different.

---

I think 3.7.2 should have "user" changed to "consumer" and to be moved to be together with 4.1.2.

By "to be together," I meant that those 2 requirements should be in the same section; I did not want to propose merging them.

Also, @tghosth commented here https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1733#issuecomment-2826707445 that he is not into this move.

Thanks for this summary Elar. My take on this is:

- 3.7.2 and 3.7.4 group well together, they would both be developed and tested together.

- 4.1.2  is more TLS configuration than redirect functionality and is usually minor TLS configuration or framework configuration
- 15.3.2 is more about SSRF protection and is usually a small library configuration flag in a HTTP client
- 4.2.2 looks more like trust boundary issues that redirect functionality

So the more I look at this, the only thing I would suggest is to put 3.7.2 and 3.7.4 next to each other instead of a small gap between them. Maybe even put those two is a different section in v3.
